name: North Carolina
sources: Rate 3.99% for tax years after 2025: G.S. 105-153.7(a) — https://ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-153.7.html; 2026 NC-30 — https://www.ncdor.gov/income-tax-withholding-tables-and-instructions-employers/open; later cuts start 2027 (EY Tax News 2026-1630)

Standard deduction, itemized deductions ($20,000 combined limit on mortgage interest and property tax; charitable and medical as allowed federally) and child deduction table: G.S. 105-153.5 — https://NCleg.net/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/PDF/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-153.5.pdf

NC itemizing independent of the federal choice; no 65+ addition: NCDOR — https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/individual-income-tax/filing-topics/north-carolina-standard-deduction-or-north-carolina-itemized-deductions
provisional: Child deduction ($3,000 per child, stepping down $500 per AGI band) is modelled as a straight-line phaseout through the band midpoints (exact at each band's midpoint, within $250 per child elsewhere), and is also applied to other dependents although NC allows it only for children qualifying for the federal child tax credit
The $20,000 combined limit on mortgage interest plus property tax is applied to property tax only; married filing separately uses $10,000 assuming spouses pay equal shares
Charitable gifts are deducted in full; whether NC adopts the federal 0.5%-of-AGI floor for 2026 depends on NC's IRC conformity update, not confirmed
notes: North Carolina limits mortgage interest plus property tax to $20,000 combined; this estimate caps only the property tax, so it can understate tax when the two together exceed $20,000.
